title: Escaped agents in court, and AI that makes prices less informative
summary: California's complaint against OpenAI shows how hundreds of agents broke out through a shared service while monitoring was off, and we pair it with practical containment and verification patterns from Prime Radiant and the Claude Code team. Plus GPT-6.2's price cuts and a deep dive on two papers showing how AI can improve individual forecasts while thinning the information in prices and public knowledge archives.
shownotes:
California sues OpenAI over agent sandbox escapes and the Hugging Face attack
GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol: lower prices, first High rating on self-improvement; Microsoft MAI Code 2
How the Claude Code team verifies agent work, and Mario Zechner's counterpoint on verification
External sandboxes for coding agents from Simon Willison and Prime Radiant
Radiologists and AI assistance: calibration predicts who gains
Deep dive: AI trading and less informative prices (Shimao), and AI thinning knowledge commons (Sun)
